Beginner, looking to get started. I don't have a lot of experience, but I find restoring old metal tools to be quite enjoyable. I don't own a lot of power tools (cordless drill, dremel, orbit sander) and I just can't justify dropping $200+ bucks each on a circular saw, miter saw, jigsaw, router, etc. Not to mention the small fortune I'd need to buy a drill press, bandsaw, table saw, or planer.

While my next purchase will probably be a cheap circular saw, I've seen many people highly suggest buying an old craftsman 113.xx table saw and restoring it for $50-100 as a way to avoid the initial financial hurdle of starting out. While time consuming, it seems doable even for a beginner. It got me thinking about what kinds of tools are worth getting and restoring, and what should just be bought new. Here's what I have so far in my 'I should buy it and restore it' list.

Craftsman 113.xx table saw

Stanley #4 Plane

Stanley #71 Hand Router

I've also seen a lot of 'DIY' builds, including DIY table saws by mounting a circular saw upside down, making a wood-frame disk sander, and others. The table saw looks way too dangerous to try and DIY, but the disk sander is still something I see myself doing long before purchasing one.

Finally, I also see a lot of people simply recommend purchasing something used off of craigslist/garage sales/etc, but I have absolutely no clue how to tell if something is in good shape or not, aside from really obvious broken/missing pieces. It may be easy for an experienced person who has owned a lot of these things to tell what's a good deal and what's not, but not for a beginner. Are there any tools that are relatively safe to buy used? Any you would only ever buy new?

So for anyone willing to share their knowledge, here are my questions for you:

1) What tools are worth the time to buy in rusted condition and restore? (with no prior experience)

2) What tools are safe to buy used? (for someone who can't tell how good of condition it's in)

3) Which tools would you think are safe to make yourself? (for someone who's never owned the real deal)

4) Which tools would you only ever consider buying new?

Cheers!

BTW, if anyone is interested in my current wishlist (subject to changes)
Starting tools; restoring used vs. buying new vs. DIY

It would be useful to know what sorts of project's you're contemplating, too.

Take look through old issues of Fine Woodworking and ShopNotes for some ideas on DIY stationary tools.

I also suggest you start haunting woodnet.net's forum. There are others, too. Let me know if you'd rather use .AU or .UK forums.

I might hesitate to buy tablesaw unless I could see/hear it in operation.

1) planes, chisels - rust is okay, avoid pitting though unless you have a lot of time to spend removing it. clamps, screw drivers etc - condition doesn't matter. If you see a second hand clamp, buy it before some one else does! Power tools.... some external rust is okay - you've just gotta be sure that nothing structural is fucked. I recently bought a 1984 Masport model tablesaw/joiner/sander to replace my ~2010 ryobi tablesaw. The 30 year is miles ahead of the ryobi in terms of quality, even if it looks old and tired.

2) Any sort of hand tool is probably "safe" to buy, provided you are prepared to derust it. Most powertools are probably also okay. The only ones I'd really be concerned about safety wise would be tablesaw and joiner, lathe and maybe a bandsaw. Other tools can fail (eg drill press), but usually not in a catastrophic way as long as you have safety gear on.

3) Any that you can - probably easiest things to make are mallets and various shop jigs (cross cut sled etc). Don't be fooled by the DIY tablesaws/jointers - you need some experience (imo) before you try making something as big as them... and by that point you probably already own one!

4) Sandpaper and glue. (Though actually, I have bought second hand glue - was still in the bottle though!) Very few of my tools were bought new, and none of the bigger budget items.
